editorial:
You meet Stan, a nervous con man who would rather talk his way out of trouble than throw a punch. When fraud charges send him to prison, he panics and hires a strange martial arts teacher to turn him into someone inmates will respect. The movie mixes prison jokes, slapstick fights, and a silly underdog story, so you get a goofy ride rather than a serious crime drama. Stan’s fear is funny, and his training scenes give the story a clear goal.

The action is cartoonish but easy to follow, and the cast leans into the absurd tone. Some jokes feel dated, and the prison setting is played for laughs instead of realism, so you should not expect deep drama. If you enjoy dumb, energetic comedies with martial arts gags, this is a fun late-night pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the sharpest picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Stan stops relying on fear and uses his training to protect others instead of just himself. The prison chaos settles as inmates respect him, and the story reveals that his guru’s real lesson was discipline, not violence. Stan leaves prison changed, with his wife and friends seeing a braver man, while the movie keeps its goofy tone and closes on a joke about his new confidence.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy prison comedies and martial arts gags.
